lines.text: Two landmasses. One channel between them. One point five nautical miles of water. And no second option.
At its narrowest it is two point eight kilometres across. Wide enough for most ships. Only just.
A fully loaded supertanker sits twenty point five metres underwater. The seabed is twenty five metres down. That leaves four point five metres of water under the hull.
So why not go around? The Sunda route is shallower still. Big tankers have to run east, past Lombok, through Makassar.
You cannot widen a strait. Chokepoints do not create risk. They concentrate it.
